field_name_desc:
the capability of student on research
(Evaluated by the professor) [format: integer] Value: higher --> higher research ability / capability

professor who advises this student [format: integer] Value: this value may be repetitive since one professor may advise many students in this semester
commonsense evidence:
if a professor advise > 2 students in this semester, it means this professor's research work is heavy
or: this professor's popularity on research is higher [primary key] [foreign key -> prof.prof_id]

the salary of this student. [format: text] Value: med: average salary
high: higher salary than others
low: lower salary
free: unpaid RA
the id numbe representing each student [format: integer] [primary key] [foreign key -> student.student_id]
unique id representing the course [format: integer] [primary key]

credit of the course [format: integer] Value: commonsense evidence:
higher means more important

difficulty of the course [format: integer] Value: commonsense evidence:
higher --> more difficult
smaller --> less difficult
name of the course [format: text]
email of the professor [format: text]
the first name of the professor [format: text]
gender of the professor [format: text]
the school where the professor graduated from [format: text]

the last name of the professor [format: text] Value: commonsense evidence:
full name: first name, last name

popularity of the professor [format: integer] Value: commonsense evidence:
higher --> more popular
unique id for professors [format: integer] [primary key]

the teaching ability of the professor [format: integer] Value: commonsense evidence:
higher --> more teaching ability, his / her lectures may have better quality
the id of courses [format: integer] [primary key] [foreign key -> course.course_id]

the grades that the students acquire in this course [format: text] Value: commonsense evidence:
 A: excellent -- 4
 B: good -- 3
 C: fair -- 2
 D: poorly pass -- 1
 null or empty: this student fails to pass this course
 gpa of students for this semester = sum (credits x grade) / sum (credits)
student satisfaction with the course [format: integer]
the id of students [format: integer] [primary key] [foreign key -> student.student_id]
email [format: text]
the first name of the student [format: text]
gpa [format: real]
intelligence of the student [format: integer] Value: higher --> more intelligent

the last name of the student [format: text] Value: commonsense evidence:
full name: f_name, l_name
phone number [format: text]
the unique id to identify students [format: integer] [primary key]

type of the student [format: text] Value:  TPG: taught postgraduate student(master)
 RPG: research postgraduate student (master)
 UG: undergraduate student(bachelor)
commonsense evidence:
both TPG and RPG are students pursuing a masters degree; UG are students pursuing the bachelor degree
